rows.question: How well does BERT perform on the SQuAD 2.0 dataset?

full.answer:
BERT performance on the SQuAD 2.0 dataset varies depending on the specific model implementation and evaluation setting:

*   **Google BERT**: Obtains 83.3 F1 on the SQuAD 2.0 test set (single model, English) [4].
*   **Our BERT**: Obtains 85.9 F1 on the SQuAD 2.0 test set (single model) [4].
*   **BERT-large**: Obtains 81.9 F1 on SQuAD 2.0 (single, English, large) [5].
*   **BERT-large**: Obtains 81.8 F1 on SQuAD 2.0 dev and 89.1 F1 on SQuAD 2.0 test (single model, English, large) [6].

Note: A difference in F1 scores (81.9 vs 90.9) between sources [5] and [6] is explained by the dataset version (SQuAD 2.0 vs. SQuAD 1.1).

no_stage_c67.answer: On the SQuAD 2.0 dataset, the BERT-large (Single) model achieves an EM of 80.0 and an F1 of 83.1 on the test set [4]. In comparison to the BERT baseline, SpanBERT exceeds the baseline by 2.8% F1 on SQuAD 2.0 [2].

llm_only.answer: BERT achieves an F1 score of approximately 81.1 on the SQuAD 2.0 dataset.

rows.question: How well does XLM-R do on MLQA for Hindi?

full.answer:
On the MLQA benchmark for Hindi, the performance of XLM-R models is as follows:

*   **XLM-R**: Achieves 69.2 F1 and 51.6 EM [2].
*   **XLM-RBase**: Achieves 59.4 F1 and 42.9 EM [2].

In comparison, mBERT (large) achieves 43.8 F1 and 29.7 EM on the same task [2]. XLM-R outperforms mBERT by 13.0% in F1-score and 11.1% in accuracy [4].

Note: These results are for the zero-shot setting where models are fine-tuned on the English SQuAD dataset and evaluated on the 7 languages of MLQA [2, 4].

no_stage_c67.answer: On the MLQA dataset, the XLM-R model achieves an F1 score of 51.6 and an Exact Match (EM) score of 69.2 for the Hindi (hi) language [5]. This result was obtained in a zero-shot setting where the model was fine-tuned on the English Squad dataset and evaluated on the 7 languages of MLQA [5]. The XLM-R model used for this evaluation was trained on 100 languages [3].

rows.question: Compare MuRIL and mBERT on XNLI for Hindi.

full.answer:
Performance results for MuRIL and mBERT on the XNLI task for Hindi vary across different evaluation settings:

*   **XTREME (IN) setting:** MuRIL achieves 74.1 Acc. on XNLI (test set, Hindi), while mBERT achieves 66.8 Acc. [1].
*   **XNLI (hi-tr) transliterated setting:** MuRIL achieves 68.2 Accuracy on XNLI (test set, Hindi), while mBERT achieves 39.6 Accuracy [2].
*   **XNLI (hi) standard setting:** MuRIL achieves 70.7 accuracy on XNLI (test set, Hindi), while mBERT achieves 60.5 accuracy [3].
*   **IndicXNLI task:** MuRIL achieves 76.3 accuracy on IndicXNLI (single model, Hindi), while mBERT achieves 63.9 accuracy [5].

no_stage_c67.answer:
On the XNLI dataset for Hindi (hi), MuRIL achieves an accuracy of 70.7% [5]. In comparison, mBERT achieves an accuracy of 60.5% for the same language and dataset [5]. These results are reported in the context of the XTREME (IN) benchmark [1].

Additionally, for the transliterated version of the XNLI dataset (XNLI in XTREME (IN-tr)), MuRIL achieves an accuracy of 64.7%, while mBERT achieves 39.2% [2].

llm_only.answer: MuRIL outperforms mBERT on the XNLI task for Hindi because it was specifically pre-trained on a large-scale multilingual corpus including high-resource Indian languages. While mBERT is a general multilingual model, MuRIL's specialized training on Indian languages provides it with better linguistic nuances and performance in the Hindi subset.
